verdicts.reason: A reads cleanly in the original order: headline, then a small phone, then the CTA pill, then the fine print. Its flaws are a phone so tiny the 7.2 gauge is unreadable, and fine print wrapped onto three cramped lines at nearly headline weight against the right edge. B puts the phone after the legal copy, so it reads as an afterthought jammed against the right edge, almost touching the three-line fine print. That cluster is cramped and the product is reduced to a speck, which weakens both hierarchy and fidelity.
